chunks: He (peace be upon him) said: And he was asked about the meaning of their saying: 'There is no power and no strength except with Allah':

key_terms.حَوْل: Power/ability to move from one state to another

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the phrase 'Lā ḥawla walā quwwata illā bi’llāh' in Shia theology?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) elucidates that 'no power' (hawl) refers to the transition from one state to another, while 'no strength' (quwwah) denotes the capacity to execute actions, both being entirely dependent on Allah. This explanation underscores the Shia theological balance between human agency (kasb) and divine grace, affirming that all human capability is a bestowal from God rather than an independent attribute. Such clarification reinforces the phrase's role as a comprehensive declaration of tawhid in action, linking metaphysical sovereignty with practical spiritual reliance.
